scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Equity = assets − liabilities. This is what's actually yours.
LTV = debt ÷ collateral. Your bank's leverage.
Liquidity runway = liquid reserve ÷ monthly obligations (spending + interest).
scenes.vo: Banks fail from liquidity (can't pay today) more often than from solvency (owe more than they own). Track both. Assets: everything you own, at market value: collateral, yield positions, reserves. Liabilities: everything you owe: loans, margin, any payables. Equity = assets minus liabilities. This is what's actually yours. L.T.V. = debt divided by collateral. Your bank's leverage. Liquidity runway = liquid reserve divided by monthly obligations (spending + interest).

lines: Why track liquidity separately from equity?
scenes.sub: Answer: You can be solvent and still be forced to sell at the worst time if you can't meet obligations today.
